output.brief:
The week of 26 Oct (0.41%) is inside the service's normal range. Over the prior 26 weeks the mean was 0.354% and the upper edge of the normal band was 0.482%. Three earlier weeks went above 0.41%, and all three were investigated with no fault found. The error-budget burn was 0.82x, well under the 2x paging threshold. Bookings completion and retry success did not move, and no customers complained. The dashboard count matches raw logs, so the rise is not a counting artefact.

The "new pods error twice as often" comparison reflects cache warm-up on any freshly started pod. The same gap appeared in all five recent rollouts, including a config-only redeploy, and it added only 10–20 errors. It says nothing about v4.18 specifically.

I'm fairly sure a rollback isn't justified. I did not test the replica move or partner-sync traffic, so those remain unruled out, though neither is needed to explain a within-normal week.

Next steps: don't roll back. Don't mute the alerting. Note the week at ops review and run the standard check on the following week. If next week exceeds 0.48% or the page fires, investigate then, starting with the replica and partner-sync timing.
